  404 "Location not found in this book's world") → the location's POI store (none → 409) → `canUpdate(store)` (403). Nothing is
  written before the last check passes; every refusal path is asserted write-free by `TestPbPromoteElement`.
- **`store.items`, not `store.inventory`.** The design's "`ItemUtil.addNewInventory` shape" would write an `olio.inventoryEntry`;
  the compose reader (P4-3 `readLocationItems`) and §7.2 rule 4 both read the `store.items` participation, so that is what promote
  enrols via `AccessPoint.member(user, store, "items", item, null, true)` (192 a). A refusal is a 500 with the item left in the
  world Items group and no `MemberUtil` fallback; the retry reuses it by name (192 h).
- **Reuse before create.** An already-linked element whose item still exists returns `reused` and writes nothing (a link to a
  deleted item — read back as an id-only stub — re-promotes with a warning). Otherwise the element description is matched
  whole-word against the store's items (`matchItem`, P4-3) and then by exact name `type="prop"` in the world Items group; only
  then `createProp` as the olio principal: `name` = tidied description minus its leading article (64 chars), `description` (512),
  `type="prop"`, group = world Items, nothing else invented. Catalogue rows (`type="template"`) are never reused (192 e, g).
- **`elementText` is the compile-side text and P4-7 is its first caller.** `itemText(name, description, colours, materials)` is
  pure (`"<colour> <materials> <name>, <description> with <c1> and <c2> accents"`, lower-cased, parentheticals dropped, never
  "null"); `elementText(user, element)` loads the linked item freshly as the caller and falls back to the element's own
  description. No render/compile path reads `sceneElement.item` yet — `PbRenderPlanUtil.sceneElements` (P4-7) will (192 i).
- **Verifier finding, fixed in-task.** Run-1 live output was `elementText="dented pewter cup, a dented pewter cup"`: `itemText`
  compared the tidied description to the tidied name, but the prop's name *is* the description minus its article, so the two never
  matched. Both sides are now compared bare (`bare()` shared with `itemNameOf`); `TestPbPromoteElement.itemTextNameOnlyIsLowerCased`
  asserts the pair (and that a real description still survives the rule), and the live promote assertion, the route test and the
  live script assert `elementText` equals `"dented pewter cup"` exactly. Run 2: 15/0/0/0, 495.2 s, 10:35:12 → 10:43:33; 6/0/0/0, 26.92 s, 10:44:38 → 10:45:11; live 25/25 on the reuse path.
- **Node staleness.** The scene node goes DONE → STALE on every promote that writes the link (`PbBookUtil.markSceneNodeStale`,
  `staled` on the response; `sceneElement.item` is in `watched/v4`) — asserted by `firstPromoteCreatesThePropAndStalesTheNode`;
  a repeat promote stales nothing (192 f).
- **Measured.** No LLM and no SD call on the promote path (the fixtures' compose calls ran on the in-stack Ollama container through
  LiteLLM: `[LLM-GATE] route=litellm tier=local analysis=qwen3:8b-ctr pb=qwen3:8b-jos-ctr server=http://127.0.0.1:4000`). Promote
  itself is sub-second over REST (run 1 `10:23:40Z → 10:23:42Z` for the whole 29-check script); the JUnit class is 471 s because each
  live method builds a book + world + location + POI fixture (38–100 s each).
- **Verifier notes left (192 l, m):** `storeItems` has no `groupId` condition (bounded by the PBAC-read store's id set; 189 d
  deviation flagged, your call); `itemExists` is a raw existence check; the `createProp` read-back orphan edge; `setQuiet`'s
  framework text in a 500.

P4-7:
- **`referenced` is decided by the planner, not the compiler, and not by "has a portrait".** `PbRenderPlanUtil.actorsOf` marks a
  HERO / SUPPORTING / FOREGROUND actor (NAMED_BACKGROUND only under `REQUIRE_REFERENCE`) whose policy is not TEXT_ONLY and who has an
  approved PORTRAIT as a candidate; candidates fill `maxReferences − (hasLocationRef ? 1 : 0)` slots, REQUIRE_REFERENCE first, then
  priority, then row order. Every other candidate is `ACTOR_TEXT_ONLY` with its reason (`(no approved portrait)`, `(reference limit N)`,
  `(REQUIRE_REFERENCE not met)`); EXTRA / CROWD / BACKGROUND rows never take a slot and raise nothing. So `ACTOR_TEXT_ONLY` counts do not
  equal `N − referenced` in general — the live script derives its expected summary from `actor.referenced`, not from the degradations.
- **A character the caller cannot read keeps the row's own text.** `PbWardrobeUtil.Resolver.resolve` substitutes the row's FK stub when
  `readCharacterById` denies, and `listActors` projects that stub **with** `name`, so the planner's `!hasField(name)` test alone took the
  resolved branch and lost the row's text (`identity.text = null`). `ResolvedOutfit.characterUnread` (set `:838`) now routes it to
  `ACTOR_UNRESOLVED` — `"<row> rendered from the row's text (character <objectId> could not be read)"` — planned from the row's text
  with `characterId` = the FK's objectId (193 ff, `TestPbRenderPlanActors.case01`). A **deleted** character's FK reads back null, so that
  row is a plain text row (193 gg).
- **A composition row's handle is not a name, and a count of 1 is not spoken.** P4-5's `createActor` names every row
  `actor.<composition>.<n>` and stores `count >= 1`; the first live proof (2026-10-20 13:44) compiled
  `"…pale skin., actor.87dc0125-….1, 1 a pile of belongings"` into the SDXL prompt. `rowDisplayName` (`PbRenderPlanUtil:746`) returns
  null for a handle-named row and the count is folded only when `> 1` (`:567`); `TestPbRenderPlanActors.case01` carries a handle-named
  count-1 extra and asserts no handle and no `"1 a pile"` reaches any compiled prompt (`live-7` 3/0/0/0); live proof 3 reads
  `"…pale skin., a pile of belongings"` and scene 1's crowd row `"3 trees"` (193 tt).
- **A composition or actor-row read that throws is an `ACTOR_UNRESOLVED`, not an empty plan.** `findComposition`/`actorsOf` record
  `"The <composition of scene X | actor rows of composition Y> could not be read; the scene is planned without its actors"` (no
  actorId, BASE), which the veto set catches; a composition that does not exist still plans with no degradation (`case03`). The throwing
  path has no live test (it needs a mocked reader) — 193 kk.
- **The compilers carry no policy text and never log a prompt.** `Flux2Compiler` emits the SWUtil rule sentences only when the prompt
  speaks of a reference (strategy `DIRECT_REFERENCE` and `actor.referenced`), and "No extra people." only when no extras/crowds were
  asked for; `TestFlux2Compiler.rulesKeepTheAsciiHyphenAndCarryNoPolicyText` asserts no `bias|diversity|inclusive|representation`
  (189 c). In Phase 4 the selector is TEXT_ONLY-only, so every live FLUX.2 prompt lists all actors as text (193 l). A referenced actor
  in a background role keeps its ordinal in the background sentence, full and detail-dropped alike (verifier should-fix, 193 nn —
  unreachable before Phase 5, tested pure).
- **Budget drops name what they dropped.** `CompilerSupport.recordDrop` writes `"<WHAT> dropped: <items> (<over> tokens over budget
  <budget>)"` per step (ELEM_LOW → ELEM_MEDIUM → EXTRAS → ACTOR_BG detail → MAIN cut at sentence then word boundaries); a prompt still
  over budget with nothing left to drop is recorded uncut (`OVER_BUDGET_UNCUT`). Every `PROMPT_TRUNCATED` vetoes auto-approve.
- **Auto-approve reads one constant.** `PbArtifactUtil.AUTO_APPROVE_VETO_CODES` = `{ACTOR_UNRESOLVED, ACTOR_FAILED, LOCATION_TEXT_ONLY,
  PROMPT_TRUNCATED, COMPOSED_OUT_OF_ORDER}`; a known code outside it (`ACTOR_TEXT_ONLY`, `MODEL_SUBSTITUTED`, `QA_WARN`) is waived; an
  unknown or free-form entry (the `"upscale: …"` pseudo-entry) still vetoes (`TestPbAutoApprove.case08/09`). `REQUIRE_REFERENCE` not
  met is `ACTOR_TEXT_ONLY` and therefore waived — 193 mm, yours.
- **Empty lists are absent on the wire.** Every PictureBook route serialises through `JSONUtil.exportObject` (`Include.NON_EMPTY`), so a
  plan with no element rows answers with no `elements` member — measured live 2026-10-20 (`C:/tmp/p47-plan-live.log`). Consumers (the
  live script, P4-9's inspector) default `actors`/`elements`/`degradations` to `[]` (193 ss).
- **With the SD server unreachable every `/plan` costs ~85 s.** `PbModelPolicy.applyForStyle` → `IllustrationModelPolicy.apply` →
  `SwarmModelInventory.forServer` → `SDUtil.listModelsOrNull` pays the JDK's ~42 s `ConnectException` wait to `.39` once for the LOCATION
  pick and once for SCENE_DIRECT (`C:/tmp/p47-tomcat-live2.txt`); no negative inventory cache (193 ww). The plan is still correct — both
  picks degrade to `MODEL_SUBSTITUTED "Model for <task> is unresolved: INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE (…)"` and actors, elements, intent,
  summary and the compiled BASE are unaffected; `ModelResolver.addDegradation` degrades the pick rather than throwing. The live script
  allows 300 s per plan call; a full run is ~7 min.
- **Measured.** No SD call anywhere in P4-7 (`.39` down; `TestPbRenderPlanActors` points SD at `http://127.0.0.1:1`); the fixtures' compose
  calls ran on the in-stack Ollama container through LiteLLM (`[LLM-GATE] route=litellm tier=local analysis=qwen3:8b-ctr

**P4-8 (2026-10-21) — Service7 row routes + ChapBook page-composition switch.** Facts, not design changes; §27's actor/element CRUD
rows and §24's page mapping are implemented as written, with the as-built notes in design §8/§24/§27 and the judgments in §6.C 194.
- **The row API is row-level end to end.** Every board write is one PATCH/create/delete against the row itself (`PbComposeUtil`
  :2008–:2372, field-name `patchOf`), never a composition-level write that carries rows; the composition is touched separately by
  `touchEdited` (`userEdited`, `source=USER`, `revision`+1, `markSceneNodeStale`). The route DTOs are P4-5's flat `x/y/w/h` shape,
  not the plan's `box:{}` (194 m); the wire omits empty lists (`JSONUtil` `NON_EMPTY`, 193 ss) so consumers default `actors`/
  `elements` to `[]`. A live round trip of PATCH → +actor → PATCH actor → +element → PATCH element → DELETE actor → DELETE element
  → PATCH ends exactly eight revisions up (`TestPbCompositionRows.revisionCountsEveryWrite`; live proof **83 PASS / 0 FAIL**).
- **A defect of mine, caught by the tests, fixed before any deploy (194 dd):** `checkKeys` tested `refused` before `alsoAllowed`, so
  `POST …/actor` with `characterObjectId` was always 400. `TestPbCompositionRows.addActorWithCharacterAndWithDescription` found it
  (`rows-1`, `rows-2`, `rows-4` red); `rows-5` green on the fix.
- **Page compositions key on the book's group, not the scene's (architect must-fix, 194 t).** Both the lazy create
  (`getCreatePageComposition`) and the executor's find (`findPageComposition`) read `book.groupId`; a scene in a chapter group would
  otherwise have written where `PbRenderPlanUtil.findComposition` and the board never look. Verified by
  `TestChapBookPageComposition` (the composition is found by scene + book group).
- **Stale before the second write (architect must-fix, 194 s).** `markSceneNodeStale` runs between the scene patch and the
  composition write, so a refused second write still leaves the page STALE (`TestChapBookPageComposition.staleBeforeSecondWrite`).
- **A partial write is a 500 that says so (verifier should-fix, 194 ee).** `setSceneLandscapePrompt` no longer returns false when the
  scene copy landed and the composition did not; `PUT /chap-book/scene/{id}/prompt` answers 500 "Scene <id> sdPrompt persisted but
  its page composition was not: …" through `errorResponse`. The pre-P4-8 `false` (scene update returned null) is unchanged.

  not the no-prompt 409 but the resolver's 503 after the plan was built; the persisted `renderPlan` carries the composition prompt
  verbatim as the location text and inside the compiled BASE prompt (`executeChapBookPageFallsBackToCompositionPrompt`, 272 ms).

**P4-9 (2026-10-22) — Ux752 board + wardrobe.** Facts, not design changes; §26's board, wardrobe panel and reader chips are built as
written, with the as-built notes in design §26 and the judgments in §6.C 197. No backend change in this task.
- **The REST helpers live in `workflows/pictureBookWorkflow.js`** (`getSceneComposition` :1428 … `setDefaultApparel` :1634), beside the
  Phase 2/3 PB helpers, not in `core/am7client.js`; `components/PbPlanInspector.js`, `core/am7client.js` and `components/dialogCore.js`
  are untouched (mtimes 2026-10-17 / 2026-10-11 / 2026-09-26). The board is `features/pictureBookCompose.js` (new, LF, 1295 lines) on
  the sub-route `#!/picture-book/{book}/compose[/{scene}]` — two route entries (`:1282`, `:1287`) because Mithril has no optional
  route-parameter syntax — spread into `features/pictureBook.js`'s route table (`:2330`) and reached from the reader by `pb2-compose-link`.
- **Every board write is a delta PATCH of the changed keys only** against the P4-8 row routes (`saveCompositionKeys` :417, `saveActor`
  :447, `saveElement` :472); an unchanged Save makes no request. The board re-reads the composition after each write and reseeds its row
  drafts from the server rows (197 z). The Playwright default tier records the wire (`recordWrites`) and asserts the PATCH bodies
  carry only the edited keys and that the server's refusals surface verbatim (400 `settingText` non-string, 400 `shotType` listing the
  values).
- **The board must send a `chatConfigName` on every compose path.** With none, the server resolves the shared library `contentAnalysis`
  → `generalChat` connection, which on this stack has no LiteLLM key (§6.G 4), and the compose job completes with `source=MIGRATED`,
  0 actors — no error reaches the page (run `p49-pw-llm`, 15.6 min). The header carries one Chat Config control (`renderChatConfigControl`
  :554; `ObjectPicker.openLibrary({libraryType:'chatConfig'})`; default resolved library-only through `LLMConnector.resolveConfig`, never
  created) and `withChatConfig` :75 adds the pick's NAME to `composeScene`, `composeBook` and re-compose — the same shape design L1364–1368
  ratified for P4-8 (ee). The same gap stands in `features/pictureBookLocations.js` :375 (`proposeLocations` sends no config) — out of
  scope, noted, not fixed.

## 6. Blocked / waiting on Stephen

### 6.A BLOCKED — three PB-series tests red in the Objects7 gate: `9085a440` made the policy cache correct and the series grant model does not satisfy the dynamic foreign-access rules (found 2026-10-09)

**Not Phase 0 scope** (the tests date from `d3cb77c3 PB Fix`, 2026-09-21) but they are red in the module
gate, so `VERIFY_OK` is unreachable until this is decided. **No product auth code was changed** — the
remedy touches Stephen's deliberate `CachePolicyUtil` fix or the series grant design (⚠ MY JUDGMENT boundary).

```
[ERROR]   TestPbDeleteSeries.testStrangerDeniedThenOwnerDeletesWholeSeries:119 chapter 1 row
[ERROR]   TestPbListSeriesBooks.testEntitledNonOwnerSeesAllChaptersStrangerSeesNone:138 entitled non-owner must see BOTH chapters expected:<2> but was:<0>
[ERROR]   TestPbSeriesCast.testRecopyAndMergeDenyReadOnlyUserAndDoNotMutate:532 subject MUST be able to READ the chapter book (else recopy 404s before the canUpdate gate)
```
(`C:\tmp\o7-suspects-run.log`; `TestPbListSeriesBooks` run alone: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 1, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 15.74 s`.)

**Mechanism (PBAC trace, `getPolicyUtil().setTrace(true)` bracketed around
`PbServiceFacade.listSeriesBooks(writer, seriesOid)`; `C:\tmp\o7-listseries-trace.log`, bracket reverted).**
`PbBookUtil.readBook` → `AccessPoint.find` does two evaluations of `resource.policy.systemreadobject`
(policy = **ALL** rules) against the same chapter `olio.pb.book` urn:

1. Query-shape pre-check on a **narrow** read — `Scanning (objectId) … [name, groupId, objectId, organizationId, id, urn]`
   → `Adding 0 dynamic rules` → `Cache resource policy for systemReadObject-…pblistserieswriter-null-5JVy…` →
   `groupdatareadaccess … olio.universes.books.worlds.lcab51388d3.book = true` → PERMIT (trace :139-167).
2. `canRead` on the **full** record `bookRequest()` projects (`series`, `world`, `sourceData`, `sourceRange`
   populated) → `PolicyUtil.getSchemaRules` adds one `generic.policy.rule.onerequired` per populated
   identity-bearing foreign field → `Adding 4 dynamic rules` → `Cache resource policy for …-4pwE…` (a
   **different** key, :249-250). The `series` rule evaluates `ANY 0:6`: not owner (`584 == 133 = false`), not
   group owner, not `accountadministrators`, **no `/Read` on `auth.group.data:…olio.universes.books.book`**
   (the series row group, `PbOlioContextUtil.seriesRowGroupPath()`; the series Writer role is granted CRUD
   only on the chapter's own Book/Workflow/Artifacts groups by `grantSeriesRolesOnChapterGroups`), no
   `resourceReadAccess` on the series → `Policy ruled failed evaluation … ALL Pass = 1 Size = 5 = false` →
   `AUDIT DENY system.user pbListSeriesWriter to READ … olio.pb.book` (:360-377).

**Why it passed before.** Until `9085a440 Patch` (2026-10-09 09:49) `CachePolicyUtil.getResourcePolicy`
keyed the resolved policy by `name-actorUrn-token-resourceUrn`, and `policyCache` was never cleared
(`clearCache()`/`checkCache()` did not touch it). Evaluations 1 and 2 share actor and urn, so the
0-dynamic-rule policy cached by the narrow pre-check answered the full `canRead`: **the foreign-access rules
never fired on any `AccessPoint.find`.** `9085a440` keys by `resource.hash()` precisely to stop that
("keyed by urn, the first request's rule set answered every later one on that record") — and nothing else in
`git diff d3cb77c3 HEAD` on `PolicyUtil`/`AuthorizationUtil`/`PbOlioContextUtil`/`PbBookUtil` restricts
anything (the `PolicyUtil` changes only *relax* via `access.policies.bind`, which `olio.pb.book` does not
declare; the `PbOlioContextUtil` diff is the additive health audit; series grants are unchanged). So the
three tests were green only because the cache masked the rules; they are now exercising the rules as
designed, and the series grant model does not satisfy them.

**The same rule set explains all three failures, and two are product paths, not test artefacts:**
- `TestPbListSeriesBooks` — a series **Writer** who is not the owner cannot read any chapter (N4
  whole-series canvas: `listSeriesBooks` returns `[]` for every collaborator).
- `TestPbDeleteSeries:119` — the **olio principal** (`olioUser`, owner of every series/world/chapter row)
  cannot `readBook` a chapter because the chapter's `sourceData` is the author's private
  `data.data` (`/home/pbListSeriesOwner/PbListSeriesData`, ownerId 583) and `sourceRange` is owner 583 too.
  Series delete runs as the olio principal, so whole-series delete is affected in product.
- `TestPbSeriesCast:532` — a subject with a **direct Read grant on the chapter's Book group** still cannot
  read the chapter (same `series` + `sourceData` rules).

**Remedy options — your call; none applied:**
1. **Grant design.** Have `grantSeriesRolesOnChapterGroups` / `newSeriesConfiguration` also grant the series
   Writer+Admin roles (and the universe Reader) `Read` on the series row group (`/Olio/Universes/Books/Book`)
   — fixes the `series` rule, but **not** `sourceData`/`sourceRange`, which live in the author's home
   directory: a collaborator would additionally need Read on the author's manuscript, and the olio principal
   would too. That is a data-sharing decision (should a chapter's existence be visible to someone who may not
   read its manuscript?).
2. **Read-path projection.** Make `PbBookUtil.readBook`'s authorizing read project foreign fields as
   id-only references (no populated nested records → `isIdentityRecord` false → no dynamic rule), then populate
   the linkage DTO from the already-authorized record. Keeps today's "entitled by the chapter's own group"
   semantics; the collaborator sees the linked records' identity/common fields without a per-record read check
   on them. Smallest change, but it is a deliberate narrowing of the foreign-access rule for this model.
3. **Rule semantics.** Decide in `PolicyUtil.getSchemaRules` which foreign fields impose a read rule (e.g.
   only fields the model marks, or only when the linked record is in a different group than the parent).
   Engine-level — yours.

Until decided: these three stay red in the module gate and are reported, not closed as "pre-existing".
If you want option 2 as a Phase 0 stopgap, say so and it gets a test (`listSeriesBooks` as Writer/olio
principal/direct-grant subject, with the stranger still denied).

### 6.F RESOLVED 2026-10-12 (P1-12 group 5, §8.12, remedy (a); was waiting on Stephen) — `TestPictureBookWorkflow.TestFreshCharacterSubRecordsAndPortraitRender` fails alone: the test creates characters where the W3 resolver no longer looks (found 2026-10-09)

**Not Phase 0 scope and not caused by Slices A/B** (`git diff` of `PictureBookUtil.java` touches neither
`resolveSceneCharacter`, `listCharacters` nor `charsGroupPath`), but it is one of the red tests in the
module gate, so it is reported here rather than closed as "pre-existing". Solo-run output verbatim in §4.1.

**Mechanism (confirmed in `am7db` after the solo run, recursive-CTE path over `a7_auth_group_0_1.parentid`
joined to `a7_olio_charperson_0_1.groupid`):**
```
11170 | home/pbCustomTestUser/Data/PictureBooks/PB2 Fresh Character Book             | 0
11172 | home/pbCustomTestUser/Data/PictureBooks/PB2 Fresh Character Book/Characters  | 2   Jideon, Touvier
11171 | home/pbCustomTestUser/Data/PictureBooks/PB2 Fresh Character Book/Scenes      | 0
 8079 | Olio/Universes/Books/Worlds/pb2-fresh-character-book                          | 0
 8083 | Olio/Universes/Books/Worlds/pb2-fresh-character-book/Population               | 0
```
1. The test (`TestPictureBookWorkflow.java:615`) builds the book with the **8-arg legacy
   `createFromScenes`** (`PictureBookUtil.java:9024`), which delegates to the 9-arg overload with
   `pb2BookObjectId=null`; on that path (`:9147-9154`) `groupName = effectiveBookName`, `ensureBookGroup`,
   `charsGroup = ensureSubGroup(bookGroupPath, "Characters")` — so `createCharPerson` writes both charPersons
   into the PB1 group `<book>/Characters` (id 11172). The test's own javadoc (`:866-869`) documents this
   deliberately: "the fresh-character case uses the 8-arg legacy createFromScenes, which keys the PB1 group on
   the book name". `listCharacters` (`:11006`) still finds them there (legacy `{bookGroupPath}/Characters`
   fallback), which is why `assertSubRecordsPersisted` passes and `createFromScenes created 2 character(s)
   from scratch` is logged.
2. The render then calls `generateSceneImage(…, params(slug, true, FIXED_SEED), "SWARM", …)`, and
   `resolveSceneCharacter` (`:2935`) → `findSceneCharacterGroups` (`:2889`) → `findBookPopulationGroup` (`:2686`)
   searches **only** the book world's `Population` group (id 8083, 0 rows). The comment at `:2956-2960` is
   explicit — Stephen's commit `2fe062a3` (2026-09-20, "Mark feat prep", W3): *"characters live ONLY in the book
   WORLD's Population group. createFromScenes is now a single path and createCharPerson (B4) routes every book's
   characters into that Population group, so the legacy PB1 <book>/Characters probe has been removed"*. The
   Population group is found (no "No book-world Population group found" warning), it is simply empty, so both
   names fall through all four `findCharPersonByNameInGroup` passes → `Could not resolve scene character` →
   `Stage 1 complete: 0 portraits generated` → no PORTRAIT nodes → `:710` fails.

So the W3 statement "createFromScenes is now a single path" is true only for the 9-arg PB2 overload; the
8-arg legacy overload still exists and still routes characters to `<book>/Characters`, and this test has
been using it since before W3. Deterministic; the earlier "re-run alone" classification in §4.1 was wrong for
this test (it was right for `TestStepBudgetComparison`).

**Remedy options — your call; none applied (⚠ MY JUDGMENT boundary — both touch a path you changed in W3):**

- **(b) Restore the legacy `<book>/Characters` probe** in `resolveSceneCharacter` as a fallback after the

### 6.C Decisions already made under auto mode

Items 2–7 are ⚠ MY JUDGMENT calls made under auto mode after the architect review
(2026-10-09; verdict: P0-1/3/4/7/8/9/10 APPROVED, P0-2/5/6/11 CHANGES-NEEDED, all resolved below).
Say so at the phase stop if any should go the other way.

2. **P0-2 `hires` semantics.** `createImage` now honours its `hires` argument, and the refiner block
   runs only when `hires && refinerModel` is non-blank (WARN otherwise — a generic guard, per
   `feedback-model-agnostic-llm-safeguards`). Callers that passed a literal `false` while their
   config said `hires=true` (`ChapBookUtil:1876`, `PbNodeExecutor:189/:564`, `PictureBookUtil:9854`)
   now pass the effective config's `hires`, so today's config-driven behaviour is preserved except
   that a config with **no** `refinerModel` no longer runs a refiner pass at all. `OlioService:217/:643`
   left as they are unless they pass a literal.
3. **P0-5 side effects.** Adding `"default": true` to `flux2IncludeLandscapeRef` supersedes the
   "NO SCHEMA DEFAULT ON PURPOSE" note at `configModel.json:366` (rewritten). `flux2Defaults.json`'s
   `includeLandscapeRef` stays as the fallback for *sparse* records (field absent → `Flux2Defaults`),
   documented as unreachable for schema-built configs. `PbGraphUtil.PB_PIPELINE_VERSION` is bumped
   because `configModel.json:8` says a changed default must bump it. Every API-/test-created FLUX.2
   book now pays the third (landscape) reference unless it opts out; Ux752's wizard still pins
   `flux2IncludeLandscapeRef=false` + `skipLandscape=true` (`pictureBook.js:243-244`) — left as is.
4. **P0-6 test seam.** No static test toggle in production code (`feedback-test-only-instrumentation`).
   The landscape stage is factored so the test can inject the failure from the test side (an `SDUtil`
   subclass supplied through a package-private overload, or a poisoned per-call landscape config);
   the subclass lives in the test.
5. **P0-8 PENDING semantics** left alone (no RUNNING stamp in Phase 0; Phase 1 §21 owns it).
6. **P0-9 `applyConfigStyle`** hosted on `SDUtil` (the style seam) rather than widening `PictureBookUtil`;
   ChapBook follows the effective config's `hires` (no forced `false`) and relies on the P0-2 guard.
7. **P0-10 transport** = new `PUT /rest/olio/chap-book/{bookObjectId}/settings` in `ChapBookService`
   (`@RolesAllowed`, transport-only, delegating to `PbBookUtil.setBookSdConfig`) with an H2 Service7
   test, instead of widening `PictureBookUtil.setBookSdConfig` (coupled to PB1 `.pictureBookMeta`).
   The client overlay is request-transient and is **not** folded into `resolveDeclaredConfig`/`configHash`.

1. **Four artifact schema fields — Phase 0 or Phase 1?** Design §23 says `attempt`, `variantIndex`,
   `reviewStatus` and `durationMs` "do not exist on `artifactModel.json` today … they are added in
   Phase 0 (§32)", but §30 row 0 (and the brief's P0 list, which reproduces it) does not name them.
   ⚠ MY JUDGMENT: **not** adding them in Phase 0; they are nullable column-backed fields (a JSON edit +
   restart per `objects7-reference.md` Path 1) and the first consumer is Phase 1's review status, so
   adding them at the start of Phase 1 loses nothing. Say if you want them in Phase 0.

**Slices C/D (2026-10-09, after the planner's plan and the architect's plan review — §4 table).**
Items 8–15 are the resolutions; 8–11 and 14 are ✓ FOLLOWING INSTRUCTIONS (rules files / architect
blocking item), 12, 13 and 15 are ⚠ MY JUDGMENT.

8. **P0-10a persistence shape** = one `olio.sd.config` row named `book-sdConfig` in the book's
   group, FK'd from `olio.pb.book.sdConfig` — the only shape the existing `foreign` FK
   (`bookModel.json:64-69`) admits; same name/group PB1's `persistBookSdConfigFk` already uses, so a
   PB1 book and a ChapBook look identical to `PbConfigUtil.bookConfig`. The create branch first
   **adopts** an existing `book-sdConfig` row in that group (`SdConfigUtil.findConfig`) before creating
   one (architect blocking item: PB1's FK patch is best-effort, so an unlinked row is reachable);
   covered by a test that pre-seeds an unlinked row and asserts no second row.
9. **Writes run as the request user via `AccessPoint`**, never the olio principal; the GET never
   writes (`architecture.md` "read paths must not create"). The REST GET reads the config via
   `AccessPoint.find` with an explicit projection, not through `ensureFullSdConfig`'s search-layer
   refetch (architect suggestion adopted).
10. **Update path** = field-name `newInstance` patch of identity + `name` (copied from the existing
    row) + the changed fields; the client's identity fields are discarded (`SD_OVERRIDE_SKIP`), so a
    client config carrying another row's `objectId`/`groupId` cannot redirect the write. Update results
    are asserted; a null result is an error, not a WARN (unlike PB1 `:2128`, left as is).
11. **P0-10b overlay never hashed.** `resolveEffectiveConfig(book, node, composite, clientOverlay)` is
    additive; `resolveDeclaredConfig`/`configHash` are untouched. The overlay sits **below** the page
    `configOverride`. It must never be called from `PbNodeExecutor` (a transient overlay that changes
    the image but not the hash would be a §11.1 drift blind spot once ChapBook pages are graph nodes in
    Phase 1) — recorded in the overload's javadoc and here; Phase 1 must either persist the overlay into
    the node's `configOverride` or reject it.
12. ⚠ **Render persists settings.** In the Ux752 ChapBook render dialog, "Render" first `PUT`s
    `/settings` when the book-level config has unsaved edits, then sends only the per-render delta as
    `sdConfig` on the render POST. A render click therefore saves book settings as a side effect. Chosen
    so that what the user sees in the dialog is what the stored config says (G-32: the client config must
    not silently become the whole config). If you want render to stay side-effect free (explicit Save
    only), say so.
    **Made precise for P0-10d (2026-10-09, planner + architect review, both CHANGES-NEEDED → resolved):**
    (a) "unsaved edits" on a book that has **no** `book-sdConfig` row yet means the **whole seeded
    entity** — the dialog seeds from the user's `sdcfg-default` preference, but the server render chain
    (`PbConfigUtil.mergeTiers` `:371-381`: schema defaults → stored book row → client overlay → scene
    override) has **no** user-preference tier, so sending only the touched fields would render with
    `configModel.json` defaults while the dialog showed `sdcfg-default` — the exact mismatch item 12
    exists to prevent. So the **first** Save/Render/Regenerate/Re-render of a row-less book PUTs the
    full seeded entity (the same thing PB2 `persistBookSettings`, `pictureBook.js:1282-1291`, already
    does), and from then on only `inst.changes` fields go on the wire. Consequence: once a row exists a
    later change to the user's `sdcfg-default` does **not** propagate to that book — say if you want it

    and `attributes` are stripped client-side before PUT **only** to keep the wire sparse; the server's
    `BOOK_SD_CONFIG_SKIP` / `SD_OVERRIDE_SKIP` stay authoritative. (c) Explicit Save buttons exist too
    (`cb-save-book-sd` in the review toolbar panel, `cb-dialog-save-book-sd` in the render dialog), so
    "explicit Save only" is a one-line change (drop the PUT from the render sync) if you want it.

    would mislabel an internal error as the caller's fault. The invariant the reviewer asked for —

    in `degradations[]`. Recorded so Phase 4 picks it up; nothing to ratify unless you want Phase 1 to

    one-line change, outside every P1 task; say the word.

48. ⚠ **P1-6: a render request with nothing to execute is a 409, not an empty COMPLETED run.** After
    the plan (terminals + upstream closure, filtered to executable, unpinned, PENDING/READY/STALE/FAILED)
    is empty, `PbRenderJobUtil.submit` throws 409 "Nothing to render: every node of this scene is current
    (N reused, M pinned)" and writes no run. Rationale: a run row that executed nothing is noise in
    `workflow.lastRun` and in the Ux's run history, and the message tells the user why the button did
    nothing. Alternative was a zero-stage COMPLETED run. Change it if you want the run row.

49. ⚠ **P1-6: `run.requestedNodeIds` records the execution set, not the terminals.** The design says
    "the nodes requested"; I store the nodes this run will actually execute, in topological order, so a
    P1-7 resume re-plans from exactly what was asked of this run and the Ux can show "3 of 7 stages". The
    terminal(s) are in the facade DTO (`sceneObjectId` / `sceneCount`), not on the run. If you want the
    terminals persisted too, a `terminalNodeIds` list field on `olio.pb.run` is an additive P1-7 change.

50. ⚠ **P1-6: FAILED nodes are retried by a render request** (effective status FAILED ∈ the execute set).
    A render request is the user's retry; the previous failure is in `lastError` until the retry
    overwrites it. SKIPPED stays skipped (it is a decision, not an outcome).

51. ⚠ **P1-6: a pinned producer is "satisfied" for planning whatever its status.** A pinned STALE
    portrait is not re-rendered when its scene is requested; the scene composes with the pinned artifact
    (`findSelected`). This is what "pinning means do not replace this artifact" means in §10; the stale
    badge still shows on the pinned node so the user sees why.

52. ⚠ **P1-6: lane permits are acquired per SD stage, not per run.** A 6-stage run releases the GPU
    between its stages, so two runs from two users interleave rather than one starving the other; the
    cost is that one run's wall-clock can stretch when another is active. Permit count is
    `pb.render.sdPermits` (default 1), read once at boot; declared in `WEB-INF/web.xml`,
    `docker/web.xml.template` (`${PB_RENDER_SD_PERMITS}`), `docker/entrypoint.sh` and
    `docker-compose.yml`, alongside the keys P1-8 will add. Non-PB `SDUtil` callers (OlioService
    reimage, ChapBook v1) do not take the lane (architect Q5 statement 5).

53. ⚠ **P1-6: a claim race leaves a FAILED run row.** `submit` opens the run before `tryClaim` (the claim
    is keyed by the run's objectId), so in the narrow window where two requests pass the pre-check and
    one loses the claim, the loser's run is closed FAILED "Node X is being rendered by run Y" and the
    request gets 409. The row is honest (the request was made and refused). A 429 (job cap) or a null
    submit closes the run the same way. **Corrected 2026-10-11 04:40 (verifier M1):** as first landed,
    `workflow.lastRun` was written after the claim but *before* `AsyncJobRegistry.submit`, so on the
    429 / null-job / throwing-submit branches the refused FAILED run *did* displace the pointer — the
    sentence "a refused run never displaces the one in flight" was true only for the claim-conflict
    branch. Fixed: `persistLastRun` now runs after a successful submit (after `PbRunCancelRegistry
    .register`), so only an accepted run ever becomes `lastRun`. ⚠ Consequence I chose: a pointer write
    that fails *after* the job is accepted is no longer a 500 (the job already owns the run; cancelling
    it for a bookkeeping failure would be worse) — it is logged ERROR and reported on the result as
    `lastRunUpdated:false`, and the run stays reachable by its objectId. This also closes verifier L1
    (a throwing `persistLastRun` between claim and submit used to leak the claim): the only call left
    between `tryClaim` and `submit` is the `Work` constructor.

54. ⚠ **P1-6: `render-all` terminals are the scenes' nodes, not every node of the workflow.** Every
    scene's `sceneNode` is a terminal; the upstream closure brings in portraits/prompts/strips once.
    Nodes that feed no scene (an orphaned portrait of a character cut from every scene) are not
    rendered by render-all. Scenes with no node are listed in `scenesWithoutNode` and skipped; a book
    where no scene has a node is a 409.

55. ⚠ **P1-6: the sync `requestRegenerate` holds a `PbNodeInflight` claim keyed `sync:<uuid>`.** The run
    is opened inside `executeNodeRun` (Q9 freezes it), so the claim cannot be keyed by the run id; a
    request token does the same job and is released in `finally`. Conflict with an async run → 409
    naming that run; an async submit that plans a node a sync regenerate holds → 409 naming the token.

56. ⚠ **P1-6: `cancelRun` is 409 (not 404) for a run that is terminal, already being cancelled, or has
    no job in this JVM.** The run exists and is the caller's, so 404 would lie; the three 409 messages
    say which case. A PENDING/RUNNING run with no in-flight job (another JVM's, or orphaned by a
    restart) cannot be cancelled from here and the message says it is waiting on restart recovery
    (P1-7). Cancelling through `POST /rest/job/{jobId}/cancel` (the submitter only, by `AsyncJobRegistry`'s
    owner key) flips the same flag.

57. ⚠ **P1-6: a stage cancelled mid-LLM-stream may leave `lastError` text on the node.** The executor's
    dispatch failure path stamps FAILED + `lastError` before the worker sees `progress.isCancelled()`
    and reverts the status to the recomputed value (READY/STALE). The status is right; the stale
    `lastError` is cosmetic and is overwritten by the next execution. Clearing it would be one more
    write on the cancel path; not done.

58. ⚠ **P1-6: a stored RUNNING node status wins over the drift scan in `PbRenderJobUtil.effectiveStatus`.**
    The planner asks `PbStaleUtil`'s scan for each node's effective status (drifted → STALE, else the
    scan's recomputed value, else the stored value), **except** that a node whose stored status is
    RUNNING is reported RUNNING outright and the plan refuses with 409 (§6.C item 56's "waiting on
    restart recovery" message when no claim exists in this JVM — `TestPbRenderJob.case02`). Rationale:
    the drift scan is compute-only and knows nothing about in-flight work; letting a recomputed READY
    override a stored RUNNING would let a second run execute a node another JVM (or an abandoned
    attempt, `TestPbNodeRun.case07`) is still writing. `PbStaleUtil.recomputeStatus` is untouched; P1-7's
    boot sweep is what turns an orphaned RUNNING back into READY. Alternative was to trust the scan and
    rely on the claim alone, which is per-JVM.

59. ⚠ **P1-6 Playwright fixture binds a PORTRAIT node as a ChapBook scene's `sceneNode`.**
    `pictureBookWorkflow.spec.js:1292` exercises `POST /scene/{id}/render`, which renders `scene.sceneNode`.
    The seeded book (`wfPb2BookObjectId`) is ChapBook-created, and ChapBook scenes carry no `sceneNode`
    (only `PbPipelineUtil.dualWriteScene` :844–880 and `PbHealthUtil:823` write it), so the test creates a
    PORTRAIT node bound to a hand-prompted character and PATCHes it in as the first page's `sceneNode`.
    Normally `sceneNode` is the scene's COMPOSITE; the facade (`requireSceneOfBook`) and `PbRenderJobUtil`
    plan from the node id and never check its type, so the route behaves identically. Chosen because a real
    composite needs the LLM stages the test deliberately avoids (§6.L: hand-written `sdPrompt` → clothed, no
    LLM) and because P1-9 is the task that gives ChapBook pages a graph node of their own. `TestPbRenderJob`
    case07 used the same shape through `submit` directly. The fixture leaves the scene pointing at the
    portrait node afterwards (the seeded book is a shared e2e fixture; P1-9 will rewrite `sceneNode` for every
    page on the v3 path). Alternative was to build a real composite through the P0 pipeline per run, which
    would make the exit-criterion test an LLM test.

60. ⚠ **P1-6 security review (PASS, 04:05) — H1 fixed, H2–H4 recorded, not fixed.** The reviewer's
    four hardening items and what I did with each:
    - **H1 fixed** — a FAILED `olio.pb.run` row was written (`startRun`) before `AsyncJobRegistry.submit`
      discovered the 4-per-principal cap, so a capped user hammering `render-all` grew one FAILED row per
      request. `PbRenderJobUtil.submit` now checks `AsyncJobRegistry.activeCount(user)` before the drift
      scan and before any run row exists and refuses with 429; the registry's own under-lock check at
      submit still closes the race and the existing catch still closes the run FAILED in that narrow window.
      This is P1-6's own defect, so in scope. Covered by `TestPbRenderJob` (re-run below) — no dedicated
      case fills four real jobs (each would need an SD render or a stub work item).
    - **H2 not fixed** — `e.getMessage()` of SD/HTTP exceptions lands in `run.error` / `node.lastError` /
      the job result and can carry the deployment-global SD server host:port, readable by any book
      updater. Same pattern as the P0-8 executor; a one-place sanitiser for connection-class exceptions
      is the fix. Left for your call (it is cross-cutting, not P1-6-specific).
    - **H3 not fixed** — every submit forces a drift scan (`PbStaleUtil.scan(…, true)`) plus the N+1
      `listWorkflowBindings` on the HTTP thread, including submits that 409. Update-right-gated, so
      cost-only. The H1 pre-check now skips it for a capped principal. Bound it with P1-7/P1-10 when the
      scan's TTL cache is exercised by the Ux.
    - **H4 not fixed, by design** — `PbRenderLanes` permits are deployment-global (SD servers are
      `/System` connections); one tenant's queued jobs can hold a server's lane while another waits. Not
      a tenancy guarantee and never claimed as one. The reviewer suggests an architecture-rule sentence
      saying so; I have not edited `.claude/rules/` (no user authority in a hand-back) — your call.
    - Cosmetic: the sync path's claim key `sync:<uuid>` surfaces in the 409 text as "run sync:…"
      (`PbServiceFacade.java:416-417`). Left.

62. ⚠ **P1-7: PENDING runs are swept as INTERRUPTED, not only RUNNING ones.** Design §21 says "any run
    left RUNNING". `PbRenderJobUtil.submit` writes the run PENDING *before* the registry accepts the job,
    and the pool is 2 wide, so a stop can strand a PENDING run that no worker will ever close (between
    `startRun` and `submit`, or queued). The sweep closes those too, with a distinct text ("stopped before
    this run was dispatched"), and counts them separately (`pendingInterrupted`). Dated §21 edit (a).
63. ⚠ **P1-7: the boot sweep reads with principal-less raw queries, then writes as each run's owner.**
    There is no principal at boot (`RestServiceEventListener.startup` runs before any request), and the
    runs belong to many users across organizations. `PbRecoveryUtil.sweepInterrupted` reads `olio.pb.run`
    / `olio.pb.node` through `IOSystem.getActiveContext().getSearch().findRecords` (no PBAC — the same
    idiom as `PbOrphanUtil.raw`, `PbHealthUtil.java:1259`, `SetupUtil.java:817`), resolves the owner by
    id (`getReader().read(MODEL_USER, ownerId)`) and writes through `PbGraphUtil.completeRun` /
    `persistStatus` — i.e. `AccessPoint.update` **as the owner**, never the org admin, never
    `RecordUtil`. A write PBAC refuses, or an owner that cannot be resolved, is counted (`denied`,
    `ownerUnresolved`) and listed under `problems`, never forced. The util is boot-only and test-scoped —
    not REST-reachable. **The architect (P1-7 review, ruling 3) recommended adding a rule to
    `.claude/rules/architecture.md` naming when a principal-less maintenance read is permitted (boot /
    test only; never request-reachable; writes always re-authorized as a concrete user). I did not edit
    the rules file — that is your call, not a subagent's. The candidate text is in §8.7.**
64. ⚠ **P1-7: the sweep assumes exactly one Service7 JVM per database.** A second JVM's live runs are
    indistinguishable from this JVM's dead ones, so a second sweep would interrupt them. The util logs
    this assumption on every run and skips anything in flight *in its own JVM* (`PbRunCancelRegistry.peek`
    / `PbNodeInflight.runOf`), which also makes it safe to call from a JUnit test while jobs run. Console7
    does not sweep. If you ever run two Service7 instances against one DB, the sweep needs an
    instance-id on the run (additive column) — not built.
65. ⚠ **P1-7: a graceful stop closes runs from the worker, before the boot sweep ever sees them.**
    `RestServiceEventListener.shutdown` now raises `AsyncJobRegistry.beginShutdown()` as its first act
    (before `LLMConnectionManager.shutdownAll()`), and the worker checks the flag (or a thread interrupt)
    at every stage boundary, inside the lane wait, and as the cause of a thrown stage: the node returns
    to READY (`persistStatus`, not `recomputeStatus` — nothing about its inputs changed) and the run closes
    INTERRUPTED "Interrupted by shutdown after N of M stage(s)" while the DB is still up. **Shutdown
    outranks cancel**: a job cancelled *during* a stop reads INTERRUPTED, not CANCELLED — resumable, which
    is the safer reading. `PbRenderLanes.acquire` also returns false on the flag (companion to architect
    ruling 8), so a queued job does not sit out `AsyncJobRegistry.shutdown()`'s 5 s `awaitTermination`.
    The flag is lowered again at the end of `AsyncJobRegistry.shutdown()` because `IOSystem` is
    reopenable (tests). What the flag cannot interrupt: an in-flight SD call (blocking Jersey client,
    `PictureBookUtil.java:6453`) — that node stays RUNNING, the run RUNNING, until the next boot sweep.
    Dated §21 edit (b).
66. ⚠ **P1-7: resume is a NEW run of kind `pb.resume`; the interrupted run is never rewritten.**
    `PbRenderJobUtil.resume` requires INTERRUPTED + a non-empty `requestedNodeIds` (409 otherwise; a
    pre-P1-6 run with no execution set says so), then calls `submit(..., KIND_RESUME)` with those ids as
    the requested set — the drift scan re-plans them, so DONE stages are reused and only the unfinished
    ones execute. If every requested node is already current the empty-plan 409 reads "Nothing to resume"
    rather than "Nothing to render". The response adds `resumedFromRunObjectId`. Alternative rejected:
    re-opening the INTERRUPTED run as RUNNING — it would lose the record of the interruption and fight
    `isTerminal` in `PbRunCancelRegistry`.
67. ⚠ **P1-7: `PbRecoveryUtil.sweepInterrupted(BaseRecord workflow)` takes the workflow RECORD, not
    `(Long organizationId, Long workflowId)` as the architect's ruling literally said.** A foreign
    `model` query field takes the record (`model-api.md`, "A `foreign` `model` field takes the RECORD");
    an id would silently become `workflow = null` and sweep nothing. The org is implied by the workflow.
    The unscoped `sweepInterrupted()` is what the boot listener calls; the scoped one is for tests.
68. ⚠ **P1-7: `GET /{book}/run/{runId}` returns a facade DTO, not the raw `olio.pb.run`.** `runDto`
    carries `runObjectId`, `name`, `runStatus`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `requestedNodeIds`,
    `executedNodeCount`, `failedNodeCount`, `error`, `inFlightInThisProcess`, `resumable`, and `nodes[]`
    (`nodeId`, `nodeObjectId`, `handle`, `nodeStatus` per requested id, from one `nodesById` read;
    a missing node reads `nodeStatus:"MISSING"`). No `isLastRun` (verifier B4: the Ux reads
    `workflow.lastRun` itself). It is a read — `requireBook` only, no update grant (`requireRunOfBook`
    still 404s a run of another workflow).
69. ⚠ **P1-7: the restart exit criterion is proven at the REST level, not through the Ux "Resume"
    button.** Design §21 says "the Ux offers Resume"; that affordance is P1-10's. The Playwright spec
    `e2e/pictureBookRestartRecovery.spec.js` (gated `PB_RESTART_TESTS=1`, `--workers=1`) submits a render,
    waits for RUNNING, runs `docker restart -t 0 am7test-am7-1` (the ungraceful path — `-t 0` so the
    shutdown hook does **not** get to close the run, which is the case the sweep exists for), waits for
    `/rest/setup/state` 200, re-logs in, asserts the old job is gone (404), the run reads INTERRUPTED and
    its node READY, then `POST …/resume` 202 and polls the new job to COMPLETED with an artifact. The
    "PB restart recovery:" INFO line is read from `docker logs`. The graceful path (`docker stop`, flag
    raised) is covered by JUnit (`TestPbRecovery`) against the flag directly, not by restarting Tomcat.
70. ⚠ **P1-7: `workflow.lastRun` is updated by a resume** (it is a normal accepted submit), so after a
    resume the workflow points at the `pb.resume` run and the INTERRUPTED run is reachable only by id
    (the Ux's job/run history, or `GET /{book}/run/{runId}` with the id the Ux kept). Nothing lists a
    book's runs yet — a `GET /{book}/runs` is a P1-10 question if the Ux needs history.
71. ⚠ **P1-7 security NOTE S1, recorded for you, not fixed: persisted `error`/`lastError` text is raw
    exception text and is now readable by a book *reader*.** `PbServiceFacade.runDto` returns `run.error`
    behind `requireBook` (read). The worker persists stage exception messages verbatim
    (`PbRenderJobUtil.java:631/:650/:686`), and an SD/LLM client exception can carry the backend host/URL.

80. **Docker compose trap, learned re-creating the test container for P1-8's new env:** every compose

    pinned)" because `requestSceneRender` always submits `force=false`, so the planner counts the just-unpinned current node as reused —
    the pin is lost and the promised render never happens; the same `force=false` makes the Re-render button on any unpinned current
    scene a guaranteed 409 toast (finding 2) and lets one current unpinned affected scene abort `regenerateAffected` (finding 3's
    trigger). The planner's own javadoc rules out the alternative of fabricating staleness with a STALE pre-mark (design §10 rule 3),
    and P1-9 already ratified force for the ChapBook page path, so the default is: (a) Objects7 `PbServiceFacade.requestSceneRender(user,
    book, scene, sdApiType, sdServer, boolean force)` overload, the 5-arg form delegating `false`; `requestRenderAll` untouched.

    carry the SD server/config), and rather than a new route because the P1-10 security-reviewer must not be re-run; that contract test
    is extended to admit exactly a primitive-boolean `@QueryParam` (a flag cannot name a server or a config). (c) Ux

     locked it — and the stranger's own `mustReadLocation` failed, because PBAC reads a record only when every populated foreign record is
     readable too: `PolicyUtil.getSchemaRules` (`:634-704`) adds a foreign READ pattern for every populated foreign field where
     `fs.isForeign() && fs.isFollowReference()`, `FieldSchema.followReference` defaults **true** (`FieldSchema.java:65`), only DELETE skips it,
     and `olio.pb.location.approvedRender` / `olio.pb.scene.location` / `locationVariant` carry no override. So a location whose
     `approvedRender` the reader cannot read is unreadable to the reader — a state `approveArtifact` never produces (it pins an artifact of
     the approver's own book in the same world). **Fix (test only):** the stranger renders their own book on their location, approves it by
     the product path (`PbServiceFacade.approveArtifact`), then locks; the owner's chapter-A node + artifact on that location is the
     unreadable-subject reject under test. `p34-locnode-case11.log` 1/0/0/0 (108.5 s, `BUILD SUCCESS`); full class `Tests run: 12, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 551.7 s` → `BUILD SUCCESS`, `MVN_EXIT=0`
     (`p35-locnode-full.log`). **Consequence worth knowing for P3-5/P3-6:** a scene whose `location` FK the owner cannot read is itself
     unreadable to the owner (`AUDIT DENY`, deny-as-miss in the log: `AccessPoint - One or more query fields were not or could not be
     authorized: 000-olio.pb.location--id-asc-0-0 … (objectId = "…" && organizationId = 2)`), which is why `TestPbScenePlanLocation.case05`
     has to set that FK in memory (§11.5). Not a product change; recorded as the rule.

178. ⚠ **2026-10-17 11:00 → 12:36 (code, tests, deploy, live proof), gate 18 GREEN 16:08, reviews + hardening (t)–(x) — P3-5 background-first in the plan.** Defaults taken under auto mode; asks follow. Planner →
     architect (CHANGES-NEEDED on three of eight findings → all adopted; two RECORD items → recorded here + dated design edits §12, §13,
     §19, §29) → implemented (`PbRenderPlanUtil.resolveSceneLocation`, `RenderPlan.Location` 5-arg) → `TestPbScenePlanLocation` (8 cases)
     → regressions → install / Service7 / deploy / Playwright / gate 18 / reviews (§11.5). Decisions:
     (a) **D1 — `RenderPlan.Location` keys.** `{locationId, variantId, revisionHash, renderArtifactId, description}` — the `*Id` idiom of
     the other members rather than §12's sketch `{objectId, variant, text}`; the 2-arg `Location(locationId, description)` is kept (every
     pre-P3-5 caller compiles); null members are dropped from the JSON, so a plan for a scene with no location serialises exactly as
     before. **Fact:** pre-P3-5 SCENE manifests carried the **scene's** objectId in `locationId` (`buildScenePlan` emitted
     `Location(sceneObjectId, locationText(scene))`); the first re-plan of such a scene is a one-time hash inequality, not a re-roll —
     no migration, no re-render. Dated §12 item 4.
     (b) **D2 — when `LOCATION_TEXT_ONLY` is emitted.** Only when the scene **names** a location whose render subject has no approved
     render; a scene naming none is plain text-only with no degradation (§29's default is not a shortfall — nothing promised, nothing
     missing). The architect ruled the definition belongs in design §19 — dated §19 paragraph + §29 row, not a `.claude/rules` edit.
     (c) **D3 — variant-only.** A named variant's render subject is the variant: the location's own render is never a substitute, the
     message names the variant ("No approved render for variant Night; setting described in text"), `inputs.locationVariant` carries the
     variant's hash. A scene at "the tavern at night" with only the daytime tavern approved is text-only (case04).
     (d) **D4 — option (A): the plan carries, the executor does not consume.** `renderArtifactId` rides the plan; `PbNodeExecutor`,
     `StageRequest`, `SdxlCompiler` unchanged; TEXT_ONLY does not use it as init image or reference (that is `SEQUENTIAL_INPAINT` /
     `DIRECT_REFERENCE`, Phase 5). A carried-not-consumed render is not a degradation, not `configNotApplied`, and leaves the strategy
     name/reason unchanged (case03). Dated §13 bullet; §13's "init image at low creativity" sentence stays as Phase 5's spec.
     (e) **D5 — auto-approve veto kept.** `PbArtifactUtil.autoApprove` skips a degraded attempt (`"degraded: LOCATION_TEXT_ONLY: No
     approved render for …"`), so a located scene whose place is not yet approved waits for a human — the §10 rule-5 consequence
     announced in ⚠ 175 (l). Transitional until the Phase 4 composition model decides which degradations are review-worthy. case08

188. ⚠ **2026-10-19 — gate run 22's one new red is a DB-row-order dependence in committed P3 delete code; fix proposed, NOT applied
     (product code outside P4-3's row — your call; default: apply).** `TestPbDeleteComplete#testFullFootprintStrangerDeniedOwnerDeletesSecondCall404`
     asserts the step audit records `bindingsByNode` (`:301-303`). The fixture's single binding is `node = scene node`, `sourceNode = portrait
     node`. `PbDeleteUtil.deleteWorkflowGraph` (`:207-228`) walks the workflow's nodes once and, per node, runs `bindingsByNode` →
     `bindingsBySourceNode` → `artifactsByNode`; `deleteByFk` (`:360-371`) records a step only when it found rows; `findByFk` (`:335-358`) has no
     `ORDER BY` (`olio.pb.node` declares no `sortField`; `StatementUtil.getDefaultOrderClause` returns empty), so the node order is the
     `a7_olio_pb_node_0_1_ww_2_idx` index scan's heap-TID order. When the portrait node comes first, the binding is deleted under
     `bindingsBySourceNode` and `bindingsByNode` is never recorded. Evidence: run 22's audit — `DELETE olio.pb.binding #1560` once, then node
     `#7508` before `#7507`; `am7db` workflow 2037 today has `7445@(280,23)` physically before `7444@(280,27)`; the rerun 01:25:30 → 01:27:46
     (`C:/tmp/p43-deletecomplete.log`) went 2/0/0/0 with the nodes visited scene-first. `deleteWorkflowGraph`, `deleteByFk`, `findByFk`,
     `PbGraphUtil` and the test are unchanged vs HEAD; no P4-1/P4-2/P4-3 edit touches node order (P4-1's `deleteGraphByBook` change runs
     before the workflow loop). The binding IS deleted either way — the defect is the audit's attribution and the test's reliance on it,
     i.e. a flake that will recur in any later gate.

     `bindingsByNode`, then every node's `bindingsBySourceNode`, then every node's `artifactsByNode` — so a binding consumed by a node of this
     workflow is always attributed to `bindingsByNode` regardless of row order (`deleteNodeGraph`, the per-node path, is unchanged); (2)
     `findByFk` sets `sortField = id` ascending so every delete pass and its audit are reproducible run to run. No test is weakened; the
     test's assertion becomes order-independent because the code is. Default: apply, then re-run `TestPbDeleteComplete` + `TestPbDeleteSeries`
     + `TestPbHealthStaleGraph` + `TestPbOrphanScan` (the other `deleteWorkflowGraph` callers are `PbHealthUtil.java:820` and

192. ⚠ **2026-10-20 — P4-6 (Elements → POI items: `PbComposeUtil.promoteElement`, design §7.2 rule 4) judgement calls; each
     with a default that stands unless you say otherwise.** None changes a ratified design decision. Results §12.6.

     `ItemUtil.addNewInventory` shape", but `addNewInventory` writes an `olio.inventoryEntry` row into `store.inventory` (quantities
     for the game economy), while the compose reader (`PbComposeUtil.readLocationItems`, P4-3) and the §7.2 rule 4 wording both read
     `store.items`. The promoted item is enrolled in `store.items` via `AccessPoint.member(user, store, "items", item, null, true)`
     (the same `olio.item` participation `TestPbComposeFallback` seeds) and no inventory entry is written. The row's wording is
     corrected in its Status cell. Default: `store.items` only; say the word if you also want an inventory entry.
     (b) ⚠ **Signature is `promoteElement(user, book, compositionObjectId, elementObjectId)`** (four arguments, the composition
     named explicitly) rather than the row's three-argument `(user, book, elementObjectId)`: the element is checked to belong to the
     named composition and the composition to the book (404 on either), which is the same containment chain the actor/element
     routes of P4-8 will use. Default: keep.

     P4-8 defines the board DTO. Default: keep.

     store row is gone) refuses with 409 "… has no location to hold the item" / "… has no point of interest store to hold the item"
     before any write; the design's "added to the scene's location's POI `store.items`" has nowhere to add to. Default: 409; the
     alternative (create the item in the world Items group without a store) would leave a world item no scene location holds.
     (e) ⚠ **Idempotent and reuse-by-name.** A second promote of an already-linked element returns `promoted=true, reused=true,
     created=false` with the same item and writes nothing (a link to a deleted item re-promotes with a warning). Before creating,
     the element's description is matched whole-word, case-insensitively, longest name first, against the store's existing items

     pewter cup" links the store's existing "cup", and "a cup of poison" would too. Default: keep (one cup per place beats two);

     still writes the scene only; the composition is re-synced on the next set/regenerate, and `locationText(scene,
     composition)` prefers the composition's text when it is meaningful — so a scene recovered but never re-edited

195. ⚠ **2026-10-21 — on the 194 rulings ("ee - richer body, hh - one run is fine, i - ok, jj - fix as suggested",
     15:48); each with a default that stands unless you say otherwise.** None changes a ratified design decision.
     Results §12.8.
     (a) ⚠ **The in-process `setSceneLandscapePrompt` (boolean) and `regenerateSceneLandscapePrompt` (String) keep the
     500 on a partial write; only the transport gets the richer body.** The ruling was read as a wire-shape ruling: a REST
     caller can act on `{updated:true, compositionUpdated:false, error}`, an in-process caller cannot — the ~40 call sites
     take a boolean or a String, and `renderChapBookScene` (`ChapBookUtil` ~:1782) with a `promptOverride` would otherwise
     render a page whose composition still carries the previous prompt. So the two names are wrappers over the
     `…Result` cores (`PromptWriteResult.isPartial()` → `PictureBookException(500, error)`) and the two ChapBook routes
     call the cores. Default: keep. Alternative: every in-process caller consumes the result (a ~40-site change, P4-10
     at the earliest), or the wrappers return `true` / the prompt and only log.
     (b) ⚠ **`POST …/prompt/regenerate` also answers the richer body** (`{sdPrompt, promptLocked:false, updated,
     compositionUpdated[, compositionObjectId][, error]}`), not only `PUT …/prompt` — the ruling named the prompt write;
     regenerate has the same dual write and the same partial state, and an asymmetric contract would make the P4-9 editor
     special-case one of them. Both bodies keep every pre-(ee) key (`sdPrompt`, `promptLocked`), so the current
     `chapBook.js` readers (`res.sdPrompt`, `res.promptLocked`, :451–:461 and :3186–:3190) are unaffected until P4-9
     consumes the new keys. Default: keep. Alternative: regenerate keeps `{sdPrompt, promptLocked}` and the 500.
     (c) ⚠ **194 (i) pick: no code change; the P4-8 note in design §27 is corrected.** The design row for the wardrobe
     routes (L1608, P4-5 as built) says 400; the "says 404" was my own parenthetical in the P4-8 note (L1610), now
     replaced with the correction. `PbServiceFacade.pinActorApparel` / `PbWardrobeUtil.requireApparelOfCharacter` answer
     400 as before. Default: as stated. Alternative: change the code to 404 anyway (`TestPbWardrobe` :182/:300,
     `TestPictureBookCompositionRoutes` :698 and the live proof would follow).

196. ⚠ **2026-10-21 (P4-8 live proof) — the ChapBook prompt routes write a `CHAPBOOK_PAGE` composition on a non-ChapBook scene,
     and the regenerate route depends on the library `contentAnalysis` connection when no `chatConfig` is passed.**
     (a) ⚠ Found by (ee) live run 1, which I pointed at a STORY book by mistake (`1d7c0bd9…`, scene 2642): `PUT /rest/olio/chap-book/
     scene/{id}/prompt` → `ChapBookUtil.writePageComposition` :2575 → `PbComposeUtil.getCreatePageComposition` :2412 creates the
     `page.<sceneOid>` row with no `isChapBook(book)` check, while the board GET (`PbServiceFacade.findCompositionOfScene` :4629)
     resolves purpose `SCENE` for a STORY book — so the new row is never read, and the scene now carries two compositions (id 30
     `SCENE`, id 32 `CHAPBOOK_PAGE`). Pre-P4-8 the same call wrote only the scene copy. Ux752 calls these routes only from the
     ChapBook editor, so no user path reaches it today. The stray row 32 (`517c94de-…`) was removed 2026-10-21 ~20:38 over REST as
     `e2etest_shared` (`DELETE /rest/model/olio.pb.composition/{oid}` → `true`; `a7_olio_pb_composition_0_1` count 0); the STORY
     scene's own SCENE composition (id 30) is untouched. **Default: leave for P4-10** with the scene-copy retirement — 193 (o) decides
     what a prompt write on a STORY scene means (per-scene `promptOverride` on the SCENE row, or nothing), and that decision picks
     the purpose the routes write. Alternative: refuse now — `409 "Scene <id> is not a ChapBook page"` from both prompt routes when
     `!isChapBook(book)`, refusing the whole write (scene copy included).
     (b) ⚠ `POST …/prompt/regenerate` with no `chatConfig` in the body resolves `ChapBookUtil.resolveDefaultChatConfig(user)` = the
     shared chat library (`contentAnalysis` → `generalChat` → first library config) before any user-owned config; on the Docker stack
     `contentAnalysis` points at `http://litellm:4000` / `gpt-5.6-terra` with no key, so the call 401s and the route answers
     `500 "The landscape-prompt LLM did not produce a usable prompt for scene <id>"` (live run 2), and `/chap-book/create`'s per-page
     landscape-prompt calls fall back to the stub prompt. That is §6.G 4 (yours; `chapBookConfigPanel.spec.js` :165–:168 says the
     same). The live proof and the specs pass `{chatConfig: "e2e-chapbook-llm"}` from `ensureChatConfig()`. Default: no code change —
     recorded so P4-9's editor keeps sending the user's chosen `chatConfig` name as `chapBook.js` :451 does today. Alternative: have
     `resolveDefaultChatConfig` prefer a user-owned config over the library one.

198. ⚠ **2026-10-22 (P4-10 — migration one-off, planner wiring, scene-copy retirement, 197 jj) — judgments taken while building
     it; results in §12.10.** Defaults applied as built; each one is a plain question at phase end. Nothing here changes a
     ratified design decision; (a) is the one that reads the §24 word "retire" narrowly and is the first to ask about.
     (a) ⚠ **"Retire the scene copy" = flip the authority, keep the fields as a server-maintained mirror; nothing is deleted.**
     `olio.pb.scene.sdPrompt` / `promptLocked` / `configOverride` stay in the model and are written by the server after every
     composition write (`PbBookUtil.mirrorCompositionOntoScene` :991 — one PATCH of only the differing fields, blank ≡ null, never
     throws, a refused write returns false and is reported by the caller). Why not delete: `chapBook.js` reads `scene.sdPrompt` on
     every page (the P4-8 body carries it), the v1 render path (`ChapBookUtil.renderResolvedScene`, §28.1 lifecycle) reads it,
     `PbWatchedFields` hashes it for drift, and `PbConfigUtil.mergeTiers` :415 reads the scene tier — four readers that would each
     need a composition lookup and a PBAC path of their own. Default: accept; delete the three fields in Phase 5 once every reader
     reads the composition. Alternative: delete now and route the four readers (a schema change on a populated table; §28.1 says
     disable → verify → remove).
     (b) ⚠ **Migration seam and semantics.** `PbMigrationUtil.migrateCompositions(user, book, scenes)` :703 (the class existed for
     the P1 migrations — extended, not new, despite the §1 row's "new") runs inside `PbComposeJobUtil.composeNow` :507–:526 BEFORE
     the LLM loop, as the job's user through `AccessPoint`, story books only (a ChapBook returns an empty result with a warning —
     its pages get their composition on the first prompt write, P4-8). Per scene without a SCENE composition in the BOOK's group:
     `composeMigrated(user, book, scene, false)` → `source=MIGRATED`, scene setting/action/mood → `settingText`/`action`/`mood`,
     `sdPrompt` → `promptOverride`, `promptLocked` and `configOverride` copied. Existing compositions are counted (`skippedExisting`,
     `skippedUserEdited`) and never touched; a second run creates nothing. The job result carries `migration` (`toMap()`: `scanned,
     created, skippedExisting, skippedUserEdited, failed, tagsPinned, tagsSkippedPinned, tagsAmbiguous, warnings`; `null` for a
     ChapBook; `{error}` when the pass itself threw) and the summary log line ends `", N migrated composition(s) created"`.
     Consequence of running first: `needsCompose` is true for MIGRATED && !userEdited, and `persist` on an EXISTING composition never
     patches `promptOverride`/`promptLocked`/`configOverride`/`props`, so the LLM recompose that follows keeps the legacy prompt,
     lock and config — and an LLM failure on a migrated scene is now a `hardFailure` ("existing composition left untouched"), no
     longer a `migratedFallback`. Default: accept. Alternative: a separate `POST …/migrate` route (one more authorized write surface
     for a one-off that the first compose already performs).
     (c) ⚠ **`PbWardrobeUtil.migrateSceneTags(user, book)` runs inside the same pass**, after the composition loop when `scanned > 0`,
     wrapped non-fatal (its counts fold into `tagsPinned`/`tagsSkippedPinned`/`tagsAmbiguous`, a throw becomes a warning). Default:
     accept. Alternative: keep the two migrations on separate seams.
     (d) ⚠ **Group alignment (design N-1): every composition is created in the BOOK's group.** `PbComposeUtil.openContext` :706 now
     reads `ctx.book.groupId` (was the scene's) and answers 409 "Book <slug> has no group"; `PbComposeJobUtil` :567 likewise. A
     chapter-group scene (P4-8's finding) would otherwise put the row where the board, the planner and the executors never look.
     Default: accept.
     (e) ⚠ **`createComposition` :1751 copies `configOverride` for EVERY source** (LLM, USER, MIGRATED); `sdPrompt` → `promptOverride`
     and `promptLocked` are copied for MIGRATED only (an LLM/USER compose must not inherit a legacy prompt as a board direction).
     Default: accept.
     (f) ⚠ **The composition config tier reaches `mergeTiers` through the node, not through `PbConfigUtil`.** The §1 row named
     `PbConfigUtil ~:415`; it is untouched. `mirrorSceneOntoNode(user, scene, node, book)` :1199 (the 3-arg form delegates) writes
     `node.configOverride` = the composition's when non-blank, else the scene's, for both purposes; and `node.promptText` = the
     composition's `promptOverride` when meaningful AND the book is a ChapBook, else `scene.sdPrompt`. So the hashed
     `resolveDeclaredConfig` path needs no composition lookup and the order is book → scene (mirror) → composition (via node) → node
     fields as §8 asks. Default: accept. Alternative: a composition tier inside `mergeTiers` (a lookup on every hash).
     (g) ⚠ **Every prompt/config write is composition-first, then the scene mirror.** `ChapBookUtil.setSceneLandscapePromptResult`
     :2561 / `regenerateSceneLandscapePromptResult` :2724: 404 → `requireChapBookOfScene` :2541 → `writePageComposition(…, USER|LLM)`
     (null = refused → nothing written) → `mirrorCompositionOntoScene(prompt)` → `markSceneNodeStale`; the recovery path :2067 writes
     the page composition first too. `PbBookUtil.setSceneConfigOverride` :861: composition `configOverride` → scene mirror →
     `touchEdited`; a scene with no composition keeps the scene-only write. `PromptWriteResult` :2476 flips: `updated` = the
     COMPOSITION was written (`compositionUpdated` is its alias), `sceneUpdated` is the mirror, `isPartial() = updated &&
     !sceneUpdated`, message "Page composition <oid> persisted but scene <id> sdPrompt was not: the scene mirror write was refused";
     the in-process setters still throw 500 on a partial. A bookless scene is now a **500** "Scene <oid> has no readable book"

     (h) ⚠ **A STORY scene on the ChapBook prompt routes is 409** "Scene <oid> belongs to a story book; edit its composition board
     instead" (`requireChapBookOfScene`), before the LLM call on regenerate — closes 196's unread `CHAPBOOK_PAGE`-beside-SCENE row.
     Default: accept. Alternative: route a STORY scene's prompt write to its SCENE composition's `promptOverride` (a board direction,

     for either purpose; `promptOverride`/`promptLocked` in the body → scene `sdPrompt`/`promptLocked` for CHAPBOOK_PAGE **only** (a

     (l) ⚠ **197 (jj) fixed by a display-name rule, not a null name:** `PbRenderPlanUtil.rowDisplayName` :841 strips the

     (m) ⚠ **Ux752 `promptWriteOutcome` (`chapBook.js` :480) learns the new wire shape:** `updated:false` → error toast;

     **Security-reviewer pass on P4-10 (verdict PASS with findings; acted on three, in-scope hardening of the new mirror/migration
     code; the first finding is (n) above, re-confirmed pre-existing; "no tests" was timing — test-author still running):**
     (o) ⚠ **v1 render recovery could clobber a locked composition prompt through a stale scene mirror.** `ChapBookUtil.
     resolveAndPersistScenePrompt` read only the scene, so a refused mirror (composition holds the user's locked prompt, scene does
     not) would regenerate and write back. Now `overlayPageComposition(user, book, scene)` runs first for a ChapBook: a meaningful
     `promptOverride` and its lock are copied onto the in-memory scene before `resolveScenePrompt`, so a locked composition prompt is
     what renders; and in the recovery branch the scene mirror PATCH is skipped when `writePageComposition` returns null or throws
     (`compositionLanded=false` → `recoveredPersistFailed`), so the mirror can never carry a prompt the authority refused. Call sites
     `renderResolvedScene` :1907 and `renderChapBookSummaryV3` :2306. Default: accept. Alternative: fail the render on a refused
     composition write (a view-only collaborator could then never render a page they may read).

     mirrored onto `scene.sdPrompt`; the other string keys are unchanged. Default: accept.

     **Test-author sweep B found one real regression in the P4-10 code (`TestPbRenderPlanExecutor.sceneWithoutTextIsA409BeforeRendering`
